elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form, Vendor shall provide transition assistance ... and shall export all Customer Data" — both trigger events covered, with no request precondition.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted language says "transition assistance for at least ninety days"; no six-month period appears anywhere. To meet preferred, change to "for up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause is silent on pricing for transition assistance; no "at Vendor's then-current rates" language in Section 10 or the new sentence.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall export all Customer Data to Customer within thirty days" governed by the opening temporal anchor "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format specification; the clause requires export but says nothing about a commonly used, machine-readable format.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation added; retained Section 16.5 expressly defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" and imposes no post-return deletion certificate.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Trigger is "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form", so both assistance and export duties attach to every covered exit event.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall provide transition assistance for at least ninety days" — unconditional, at or above the 90-day floor, and not conditioned on a pre-expiry request.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall export all Customer Data to Customer within thirty days", with the thirty days running from the stated expiry/termination trigger rather than from a request.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the trigger (expiry or termination), at least ninety days of assistance, and export of all Customer Data within thirty days of that trigger — the clause the Agreement previously lacked entirely.

Preferred level is incomplete on four elements: six-month duration, then-current rates, machine-readable format, and certified deletion after return. Do not claim preferred; the margin comment correctly offers it only as a discussion point.

Minimality holds. The insertion is a concise new sentence for a missing clause, deletes nothing (Sections 10.1, 10.2 and 16.5 survive verbatim), and adds no extras such as survival tails, expense allocation, or procedures. Extending the trigger to "any Order Form" tracks the Agreement's own Order Form/partial-termination structure (Section 10.1's "terminated subscription Services") rather than adding an off-checklist requirement.

Intent preserved: refunds, Deliverable delivery, access cut-off and the confidentiality return/destroy regime are untouched and do not contradict the new export duty; the pre-existing dangling reference to "Sections 11 and 15" in Section 16.5 was not created by this edit.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in the checklist): the inserted sentence is unnumbered — number it 10.3 so it is citable and so Section 16.5's Customer Data deferral can eventually be pointed at a real provision.
